subject: general
question: If a man bought 6 pencils for Rs. 5, and sold them at 5 pencils for Rs. 6, then the gain percentage is __________.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find **Gain Percentage**, equate the quantity by cross-multiplying cost and selling prices.

Quantity × Rate: **6 pencils** for **Rs. 5** (CP) and **5 pencils** for **Rs. 6** (SP).

Cross-multiply: CP = 5 × 5 = 25 and SP = 6 × 6 = 36.

Profit = 36 − 25 = 11.

Gain % = (11 ÷ 25) × 100 = **44%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → CP of 6 pencils = Rs. 5 | SP of 5 pencils = Rs. 6.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/670e57ac963d10e7231bfc8af67f870ae1ccdc514f1303470d3c0bad5c9c026d.png] 
⇒ Let total pencils be **LCM** of 6 and 5 = **30 pencils**.
⇒ CP of 30 pencils = (5 ÷ 6) × 30 = **Rs. 25**.
⇒ SP of 30 pencils = (6 ÷ 5) × 30 = **Rs. 36**.
⇒ Profit = 36 − 25 = 11.
⇒ Profit % = (11 ÷ 25) × 100 = **44%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Calculating the price of a **single unit** helps compare CP and SP easily. CP of 1 pencil = 5/6; SP of 1 pencil = 6/5.

LCM Method

Assume a total quantity equal to the **Lowest Common Multiple** of quantities to avoid fractions during calculation.</p
